facts.raw_span: A 73-year-old man
no compressive symptoms or systemic complaints
Physical examination was unremarkable
hematocrit 25.7% (normal 38–52%)
hemoglobin 12.3 g/dL (normal 13–18 g/dL)
red-cell count 3.84 × 10^6/mm^3 (normal 4.0–5.5 × 10^6/mm^3)
platelet count 88,000/mm^3 (normal 160,000–410,000/mm^3)
white-cell count 7000/mm^3 (normal 3800–8500/mm^3) with 58.3% neutrophils, 9.0% lymphocytes, and 25% eosinophils (normal 0–7%)
dysplastic megakaryocytes and erythrocytes without an increased number of blast cells
a 38-mm oval, well-encapsulated mass in the posterior mediastinum
the lesion had moderate signal intensity on both T1-weighted and T2-weighted images
the radiographic findings were not typical for neurogenic tumors

The patient has cytopenias and dysplastic cells in the bone marrow, consistent with myelodysplastic syndrome.
The patient has a well-encapsulated mass in the posterior mediastinum, which is not typical for neurogenic tumors, and the radiographic findings are consistent with thymoma.
The patient has a low hematocrit and hemoglobin level, consistent with anemia.
The patient has a low platelet count, consistent with thrombocytopenia.
The patient has an elevated eosinophil count, consistent with eosinophilia.
The patient has a mass in the posterior mediastinum, consistent with a mediastinal tumor.
The patient has a mass in the posterior mediastinum, which could be a neoplasm.
The patient has cytopenias and dysplastic cells in the bone marrow, consistent with a hematologic malignancy.
The patient has a mass in the posterior mediastinum, which could be cancer.
